Work in a room (`_data/worktrees/<repo>/<lane>`), write back to `.agents/HANDOFF.md`, and find anything else with `estate where <words>` or `estate packet <building>`.

## Who works here
The **laptop-health agent** (herdr name `LAPTOP`). Shaan runs the laptop flat out (8-10 Claude sessions, DeepSeek and
Codex workers, dev servers, test browsers, a live stream), so load storms keep coming back. This house is where the
diagnosis lives, so nobody starts from zero again. Spin the agent up with `laptop-health agent`. Any other agent can run
the same commands through the `laptop-health` skill. Shaan's words are in `.agents/source/`; they outrank this file.

## Boot
1. `laptop-health check` (10 s). It ranks the causes and exits 0 healthy, 1 degraded, 2 critical; `--json` for agents.
2. `.agents/HANDOFF.md`: the newest `## State`. `.agents/memory/MEMORY.md`: what has been measured before.
3. Follow the playbook below in order, and stop at the first cause that explains the numbers.

## The playbook (the order that has paid off)
1. **Power first.** On battery, Low Power Mode caps the M1's P-cores at 828 MHz (full speed is 3,204), so the same work
   that gives load 5-6 on the charger gives 50-100. `check` shows `P-cores 828/3204 MHz`. Fix: plug in. Turning Low
   Power Mode off on battery (`sudo pmset -b lowpowermode 0`) is Shaan's call; it drains the battery fast.
2. **Capacity.** On the charger, P-cores should reach ~3 GHz under load. If not, look at `thermal` in `check`.
3. **RAM.** 16 GB. Under ~400 MB free with several GB compressed, everything stalls on memory. `laptop-health mem`.
4. **Who makes the load.** `laptop-health load 30`: each process's share of the run queue (load average is the average
   number of threads wanting a core). "short-lived (already gone)" means process churn: go to step 5.
5. **What keeps starting processes.** `laptop-health churn 30`: every fork and exec, by source, then "what pings": the
   same command started 30+ times a minute and the agent pane that keeps starting it. A healthy laptop starts a few
   hundred a minute; 3,000-30,000 a minute is a storm. "forks never ran anything" marks a spawner that fails.
5b. **Which agent, and tell it.** `laptop-health hogs 15` groups the load by owning agent pane and matches `tips.json`
   (local whisper, uncapped vitest, full tsc, own Playwright Chrome, unqueued builds, sleep polls). `hogs --tell`
   messages those panes; `laptop-health who <pid>` walks any process up to its pane or launchd service;
   `laptop-health servers` lists every dev server with RAM, clients and owner. When you learn a new avoidable
   pattern, add it to `tips.json` (match, what, tip, measured) and run `python3 tests/test_owner.py`.
6. **Leftovers.** `laptop-health strays` (dry run), then `laptop-health clean` to stop them.
7. After any fix, run `check` again and say what changed, with the numbers.

## Rules
- **Never touch an agent.** No killing Claude, omp or Codex processes or their herdr panes, and no killing processes an
  agent is using right now. Tell Shaan which agent is heavy and let him decide; message it with the herdr method below.
- **Never free `heavy` slots held by `live-quiet`.** `sleep 2700` in a heavy slot is a deliberate hold protecting a
  live Oracle stream (`~/.cache/siso-heavy/live-quiet.pids`). `check` shows when it is active.
- **`clean` only stops the categories in `strays`**: dead-session console waiters and duplicates, dev/file servers
  whose starter is gone with no clients for 2 h+, your Chrome open with no windows, agent-launched Chromes whose owner
  is gone, the idle chrome-devtools-axi browser, and polling loops from ended Claude sessions.
- **When Shaan says a thing is his, add it to `keep.txt`** (a regex on the command line or the working folder) and run
  `python3 tests/test_keep.py`.
- **Fix it yourself.** Shaan, 25 Sep: "You should probably just sort it out yourself. That's your job." When
  another tool is cooking the laptop, make the smallest safe fix in its source (test it, restart it, prove the drop),
  then tell its owner what you changed so it is kept; `estate report` only what you cannot fix safely. The one limit
  is the agents rule above: nothing that restarts herdr or kills an agent's process without Shaan's yes. Message
  agents with `laptop-health tell` (next rule; pane ids shift, it resolves names; `herdr-send` refuses Claude panes).
- **Messaging agents: use `laptop-health tell <pane|name> "<msg>"`.** It types only when the input box is empty (text,
  a suggestion or "Press up to edit queued messages" all count as busy) and checks the line landed. Never chain a
  raw `send-text` after a read in one command: on 25 Sep that sent into a box showing text.
- **The persistent job** is `com.siso.laptop-health-watch` (launchd, every 10 min, nice 10): logs load, RAM, hogs by
  pane, pings and strays to `~/.cache/laptop-health/watch.jsonl`, tells agents with an avoidable tree over 1 core
  (each tip once an hour per pane) and stops orphaned `eslogger`s. `laptop-health watch` shows the last passes; read
  it first on boot, it is the "normal day" baseline. `watch --uninstall` stops it.
- Measure before claiming. A snapshot lies about churn; use `load` and `churn`, which sample.

## Commands
| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `health [claude\|siso\|codex\|omp] [question]` | open this agent in the current terminal; `health tab ...` in its own herdr tab `LAPTOP` |
| `laptop-health [check] [--json]` | power + Low Power Mode, P/E-core speed, load, RAM, agents, strays; ranked causes with the fix |
| `laptop-health load [secs]` | share of the load by process and kind (libproc running threads, sudo) |
| `laptop-health churn [secs]` | every fork/exec by source (eslogger, sudo) |
| `laptop-health mem` | real memory incl. compressed, by kind and biggest processes |
| `laptop-health strays [--apply K]` / `clean` | find / stop leftovers (never agents) |
| `laptop-health hogs [secs] [--tell]` | the load by owning agent pane, with waste tips; `--tell` messages them |
| `laptop-health servers` | every dev/file server: RAM, age, clients, folder, owner |
| `laptop-health disk [trees\|slim\|caches\|cargo]` | free space and trend; worktrees; reversible slimming; `cargo --run` removes Rust build caches untouched 3 h+ (watch does it under 25 GB) |
| `laptop-health who <pid>` | process chain up to its agent pane or launchd service |
| `laptop-health tell <pane\|name> "msg"` | type one line into an agent pane, only into an empty input box |
| `laptop-health watch [--install\|--uninstall\|--once]` | the 10-minute persistent job and its log |
| `bin/health-watch [--once\|status\|--install\|--uninstall]` | sample four machines every minute and wake HEALTH on sustained alerts |
| `laptop-health history` | battery vs charger timeline (pmset log) and active Claude sessions per hour |
| `laptop-health agent [...]` | same as `health tab ...` (`--print` shows the command) |

Needs passwordless `sudo` for `powermetrics`, `eslogger` and system processes in `load` (it works on this laptop).
`ps -S` and `dtrace` do not work here (System Integrity Protection).
